domains.name: Metadata and DocType runtime
domains.rationale: DocType/DocField metadata, Custom Field, Property Setter overlays, effective revision/cache invalidation and controller registry semantics are implemented with a different storage/runtime architecture but equivalent declared outcomes.

domains.name: Document lifecycle
domains.rationale: Create/save/submit/cancel/amend/delete and optimistic conflict semantics are mapped to the Document Kernel lifecycle; side effects are planned through the authoritative unit-of-work/outbox boundary.

domains.name: Naming
domains.rationale: Exact current code supports hash, classic/date series, field:, naming_series:, format:, prompt and autoincrement with tenant-scoped atomic allocation and fail-closed unsupported patterns.

domains.name: Permissions
gaps: Frappe permission_query_conditions / has_permission hook semantics are not implemented as compatible dynamic hook authorities.
Hierarchy/descendant semantics still require exact Frappe differential coverage.
domains.rationale: Role/owner/share/User Permission/permlevel server enforcement is strong, but the declared Frappe 16 permission contract includes hook-driven query/permission behavior that is not closed.

domains.name: Authentication and sessions
gaps: Audited support impersonation is explicitly missing.
Generic Frappe OAuth/API-key/token lifecycle parity is not closed; provider-specific and connector seams do not equal the full Frappe auth contract.
domains.rationale: Cookie session, CSRF, revocation, MFA and rate-limit behavior are strong, but required Frappe 16 auth/session behaviors are not all implemented.

domains.name: REST and RPC
gaps: Generic Frappe v2 arbitrary Python controller/server-script method dispatch is intentionally unavailable without a Python runtime.
Frappe v2 group_by and as_dict=false collection shapes are explicitly rejected rather than silently approximated.
Execution evidence for the new v2 compatibility tests is pending a runner; source/test wiring exists on PR #994.
domains.rationale: R7 now implements bounded /api/v2 document CRUD/list/copy/meta/count/ping/method-envelope compatibility on the same authoritative Forge services, with stronger OCC on writes. The remaining gap is narrowed to dynamic Python/server-script semantics and two unsupported collection shapes.

domains.name: Database abstraction
domains.rationale: Forge intentionally targets Cloudflare D1/Durable Objects rather than reproducing Frappe's MariaDB/PostgreSQL abstraction. R7 requires equivalent atomicity/race/replay safety, not engine compatibility.

domains.name: Query and list engine
domains.rationale: List/query behavior is implemented through a permission-aware AST/compiler with filtering, projection, ordering, pagination and search/link adapters; implementation differs from Frappe Query Builder.

domains.name: Background jobs
domains.rationale: Frappe/RQ implementation is replaced by Cloudflare Queues: canonical outbox enqueue, tenant/event dedupe, bounded exponential retry, max-retry policy and mandatory dead-letter queue. Exhausted failures are retained in the DLQ rather than Frappe's RQ failure registry; live evidence has exercised retry and durable 30/30 processing.

domains.name: Scheduler
gaps: Generic merged Frappe cron/all/daily/hourly app scheduler event semantics are not implemented; current scheduled handler primarily runs Forge maintenance.
domains.rationale: A scheduler exists operationally, but it is not equivalent to Frappe's installed-app scheduler-event composition.

domains.name: Realtime
gaps: Generic frappe.publish_realtime-compatible room authorization/order/reconnect behavior is not proven as a platform-wide authority.
domains.rationale: Realtime exists in bounded designs/verticals, but the generic Frappe framework contract is not closed.

domains.name: Caching and locks
domains.rationale: Forge intentionally does not reproduce Frappe Redis internals. Cache invalidation is revision-driven and authoritative write locking/serialization uses D1/DO semantics; R7 compares observable invalidation and mutual-exclusion outcomes.

domains.name: Files and attachments
domains.rationale: Upload, private/public access path, permission enforcement, delete and bounded file handling are implemented on R2/D1 rather than Frappe filesystem/storage adapters.

domains.name: Print and PDF
domains.rationale: Forge deliberately does not expose Frappe's binary download_pdf on Workers; it exposes rendered HTML+CSS and fails unsupported PDF generation explicitly instead of returning a fake success.

domains.name: Data import/export
gaps: Frappe background/queued Data Import status lifecycle is not exposed on the facade.
domains.rationale: CSV preview/apply/export is usable, but Frappe 16 import/export includes asynchronous lifecycle behavior that Forge has not closed.

domains.name: Workflow
gaps: Workflow email/action delivery is not complete because mail transport is absent.
Exact Frappe condition/evaluation and all workflow side-effect semantics require closure.
domains.rationale: State/transition/role actions are implemented, but the declared workflow contract includes email/actions and dynamic semantics not fully closed.

domains.name: Notifications and communications
gaps: Frappe Email notification delivery/queue semantics are not implemented because no mail transport is configured; Email intents are recorded with skipped_reason.
domains.rationale: This is a real capability gap for Frappe 16 communications semantics, not a parity success.

domains.name: Hooks and app composition
domains.rationale: Forge intentionally does not execute arbitrary Python hooks/monkey patches. Controller overrides, ordered document events and app composition are represented by versioned registries and deterministic pre-commit/outbox phases.

domains.name: Migrations and patches
gaps: Remote migration ledger crash-window/content-identity closure remains open; an applied migration must be durably and immutably attributable to exact content.
Workers-for-Platforms tenant/app rollback remains partial at provider evidence level; compatible source redeploy exists, but canonical provider rollback is not yet proven.
domains.rationale: The earlier reverse-migration requirement was incorrect: pinned Frappe 16 itself uses forward Patch Log plus transaction rollback on failed patches, not a generic reverse-patch engine. Forge already has forward append-only migrations, run journaling and backup/PITR recovery; the remaining blockers are exact remote durability/identity and provider rollback evidence.

domains.name: Desk boot and navigation
domains.rationale: Boot, workspace/desktop navigation and permission-filtered client contract are exposed through the Frappe-shaped facade and have browser/integration evidence.

domains.name: Form runtime
domains.rationale: Field rendering, depends_on/fetch behavior, trusted Client Script compatibility execution, child grids and optimistic save/conflict behavior are represented in the current form contract.

domains.name: List/report/dashboard runtime
domains.rationale: List/report execution, prepared-report fallback/async semantics, dashboard charts and number cards are exposed through the current Frappe-shaped client contract.

domains.name: Website and portal
gaps: Complete website runtime parity and customer/supplier portal/self-service flows remain open.
domains.rationale: Current exact generated verification still describes CRM/portal as metadata foundations rather than complete website/portal behavior.

domains.name: Localization
domains.rationale: The declared framework behaviors are covered semantically: tenant/user language and timezone travel in boot/session state; tenant translations override platform fallback; number/date/currency formatting is driven by boot sysdefaults with tested Frappe-style formats. Implementation is TypeScript/D1 rather than Frappe Python/Babel.

domains.name: Audit and collaboration
domains.rationale: Version history, comments, assignments/ToDo-like state, tags, shares and timeline composition are implemented with immutable/permission-aware Forge storage semantics.

domains.name: Integrations
gaps: Generic API-key/service-account/OAuth connected-app lifecycle is not fully wired.
Generic webhook/event subscription and provider-neutral production queue lifecycle remain Foundation in current evidence.
domains.rationale: Provider-specific and generic integration seams exist, but they do not yet close the full Frappe integrations contract.

domains.name: Security boundaries
domains.rationale: Forge intentionally refuses arbitrary Python safe_exec/raw SQL/implicit global state in Workers and replaces them with allowlisted DSLs, typed errors, trusted tenant identity, server-side authorization and bounded execution.

domains.name: Testing framework
domains.rationale: Frappe's internal Python unit/integration test framework is a developer implementation facility, not an observable production platform contract required for Forge clients. R7 still requires Forge-native tests/oracles for every in-scope domain.
